reference.source: runway.center is the world projection of 10.94806 N 125.01028 E from the English Wikipedia article 'Dulag Airfield' (read 2026-09-17, Plan 13b-13d design §7). headingDeg 0 is an ASSUMPTION: the article gives none; north-south along the coastal plain is used until a period photograph says otherwise. lengthM and widthM are ESTIMATES, Tacloban's carried over. Plan 13d Task 4 (2026-09-24) replaced the placeholder buildings (Tacloban's table, reused verbatim) with Dulag's own smaller set: the same Wikipedia article records the field seized 'shortly after the Leyte Landing' with the 475th Fighter Group arriving 28 October 1944, so a hastily-established fighter strip gets one small hangar (dulag-hangar-1, at the same x/z as the old placeholder's first hangar, confirmed on land by tests/sim/weapons/structures.test.ts before this change) plus one smaller maintenance shed (dulag-hangar-2, at the old placeholder's second-hangar offset, for the same reason) and nothing else -- no control tower, no third hangar, no AAA emplacement; those were Tacloban's later, larger and more permanent base. Both entries use kind 'hangar' rather than a 'hut': content buildings are strike targets (spec §2.3, BuildingObject's kind enum in src/sim/world/airfields.ts is 'hangar' | 'tower' | 'aaa' only), unlike the decorative AIRFIELD_HUTS list in src/render/scene/airfield.ts which does accept 'hut' for rendering but is never per-base content. apron and clearing stay null: a hastily-built 1944 strip plausibly had no paved apron, and null is also what keeps airfield.ts's taxiway/clutter gate (generalized this same task from `airfield.id !== 'tacloban'` to `airfield.apron !== null`) correctly silent for Dulag without a Tacloban-specific id check. side 'axis' (friendly-fire plan, 2026-09-26): H1 ruled every building 'japanese', and strike-range lists Dulag in enemyAirfields. M3 (2026-09-26): dulag-aaa-1 and -2 are GAMEPLAY CONTENT, not history — the missions spec (2026-09-25 §4.2) gives Airfield Strike a secondary AAA objective, placed west of the strip (inland) at Tacloban's emplacement size and HP; the paragraph above about a hastily-established strip with no AAA remains the historical account.
